dedupe_keys.name: global multi depth soil attributes dataset

description: The soil research team publishes harmonised global rasters of soil attributes at several near-surface depth intervals. The Geoscience Data Journal paper describes bulk density, clay, silt and sand fractions, acidity, total nitrogen, soil organic carbon and organic carbon stock. It calculates additional intervals such as 0–10, 0–15, 0–20 and 0–25 cm by interpolation or weighted averaging of source layers. Examples in the article use 30 arc-second cells. Zenodo's own DOI metadata links the dataset to the paper and states CC BY 4.0; the repository is free to access. These layers can parameterize infiltration and runoff in catchment, drainage and road-slope models, or provide broad subsurface context for buried utility exposure. They do not resolve a particular trench, foundation or local soil test. Derived depth layers inherit uncertainty and scale limits from the input grids; users should read the file README for exact raster formats, coverage masks and layer definitions before simulation. The resource complements data-isric-soilgrids-global-soil-maps, which supplies source soil properties at its own depths. No raster file was downloaded.
